record.original_question: Every n-copula C can be represented by measure-preserving transformations phi_i: [0, 1] -> [0, 1] for i = 1, ..., n through C(x1, ..., xn) = lambda(phi_1^{-1}([0, x1]) intersect ... intersect phi_n^{-1}([0, xn])), where lambda is Lebesgue measure on the Borel subsets of [0, 1]. Which particular properties of an n-copula C correspond to representations in which the n transformations are all ergodic, or all weakly mixing?

evidence.quote: Each n-copula C can be represented by means of n measure preserving transformations phi_i: [0, 1] -> [0, 1], i = 1, ..., n.
C(x1, ..., xn) = lambda(phi_1^{-1}([0, x1]) intersect ... intersect phi_n^{-1}([0, xn])).
Are there any particular properties of an n-copula C which are represented by means of n ergodic (or n weakly mixing) transformations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda$ denote Lebesgue measure on the Borel subsets of $[0,1]$. A measurable map $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ is measure-preserving if $\lambda(\varphi^{-1}(B))=\lambda(B)$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$. Such a $\varphi$ is ergodic if every Borel set $B$ with $\varphi^{-1}(B)=B$ satisfies $\lambda(B)\in\{0,1\}$, and weakly mixing if for all Borel $A,B\subseteq[0,1]$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\bigl|\lambda(\varphi^{-k}A\cap B)-\lambda(A)\lambda(B)\bigr|=0.$$

An $n$-copula is a function $C:[0,1]^n\to[0,1]$ that is the joint distribution function of an $n$-tuple of random variables each uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$. It is known that every $n$-copula $C$ admits a representation
$$C(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\lambda\bigl(\varphi_1^{-1}([0,x_1])\cap\cdots\cap\varphi_n^{-1}([0,x_n])\bigr),\qquad (x_1,\dots,x_n)\in[0,1]^n,$$
for some measure-preserving transformations $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n:[0,1]\to[0,1]$.

Characterize, in terms of intrinsic properties of the copula $C$, those $n$-copulas that admit such a representation in which all of the transformations $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n$ are ergodic. Separately, characterize those $n$-copulas admitting such a representation in which all $\varphi_i$ are weakly mixing.
